name: brown butter sage sauce
instructions:
The three-ingredient pan sauce: butter, sage, salt + pepper, cooked together in a pan until the butter browns.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- butter
- FRESH sage (needed — powdered loses its funk; see notes)
- salt and black pepper

=== PROCEDURE ===

Cook together in a pan until the butter browns and the sage crisps/infuses.
notes:
=== FRESH SAGE, NOT POWDERED ===

Fresh sage is needed over powdered — powdered sage loses its flavor/funk against the heat (the [[porkchops-with-a-sauce]] lesson).

=== VINEGAR IS CLASHING — TEMPTING, BUT NO ===

Vinegar of any kind is CLASHING, although it's tempting. If acid is wanted, use it to DEGLAZE THE MEAT instead — keep it out of the butter sauce itself.

=== OLIVE OIL IS CLASHING ===

No olive oil — this is a pure-butter sauce; oil muddies the brown-butter character.

=== DON'T FIGHT THE SOLIDIFICATION ===

It's tempting to thin it out a little, but just EXPECT IT TO SOLIDIFY BACK INTO BUTTER IN THE FRIDGE — spread it over things like butter, or melt it to use. That's the nature of the sauce, not a flaw.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[porkchops-with-a-sauce]]: variant A is this sauce built in the chop pan (brown the chops in the butter, sage in before the wine deglaze — the deglaze acid staying on the meat side, per the vinegar rule).
- [[beurre-manie]] / [[chocolate-magic-shell]]: the other keep-in-the-fridge fat preparations.
